answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, each identity locks its own refundable smart-contract bond, making multiple identities costly. Only when cryptographic proof shows conflicting commitments signed for the same task, slashing occurs. This approach is like navigating a glacier, where small changes can lead to catastrophic consequences. It requires a clear understanding of the system, like standing on a mesa, surveying the landscape. The smart-contract bond serves as a vault, securely storing and verifying identities, ensuring the integrity of the system.
